svg.title: An Exploratory Global Compute Cost Curve
svg.desc: Two electricity-only cost curves comparing standardized NVIDIA hardware everywhere with an export-constrained scenario using Huawei hardware in China. Each curve contains the same 28 regional capacity estimates, sorted by cost with identical axes. The China electricity-per-FLOP multiplier is an engineering estimate, not a measured fleet benchmark.
svg.text: An Exploratory Global Compute Cost Curve
How far can cheap power carry China in the AI race?
39,189 MW plotted in each curve · 28 regional estimates

g.text: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 in every region

svg.text: Assumptions: PUE 1.20 throughout; GB200 NVL72 180 dense-BF16 PFLOP/s per 120 kW rack. China’s 2.5× multiplier is an engineering estimate, not a metered benchmark.
Scope: selected regional estimates, not a global census. Capacity vintages differ; electricity prices effective during 2025 mix public tariffs and industrial averages.
Sources and full methodology: github.com/qrlow/compute-cost-curve · GB regions share one price proxy; all 11 capacity blocks are retained.
